topic: Move-in readiness ladder for property managers
hook: If move-in week still runs on scattered reminders, the handoff is not ready.
captionInstagram:
Why do property management move-ins still create last-minute chaos?

Because most teams treat move-in as a checklist, not a workflow with named triggers, owners, and proof. Practical property management automation should start from the signed lease, confirm utilities and documents, route exceptions, trigger resident messages, and keep the CRM or PMS current before keys are on the line.

This is where an AI front desk for property managers becomes useful beyond leasing. SMS, AI voice, document follow-up, maintenance coordination, and CRM workflows should all support one clean move-in readiness path instead of five separate reminder chains.

If your team still spends move-in week chasing insurance files, missing payments, incomplete utilities, unresolved make-ready items, or key handoff confusion, the problem is not effort. The operating workflow is weak.

slides.title: If move-in week still runs on scattered reminders,
slides.body: A clean move-in should follow one operating path from signed lease to key release, not a scramble across inboxes, texts, and sticky-note tasks.
slides.footer: Swipe for the 6 readiness rules that protect move-in day

slides.title: Signed lease should open the move-in workflow automatically.
slides.body: The clock should start from the executed lease and target date so documents, payments, utility steps, and staff ownership do not wait for someone to remember.
slides.footer: Goal: no new resident starts in an unowned queue

slides.title: Every move-in needs one required-documents lane.
slides.body: Insurance proof, IDs, utility confirmation, pet records, parking details, and policy acknowledgements should be tracked in one completion path with automatic reminders.
slides.footer: Goal: one checklist, one status, one owner

slides.title: Payment readiness should be verified before key handoff becomes a front-desk surprise.
slides.body: Deposits, first rent, fees, concessions, and payment exceptions should resolve in advance so staff are not negotiating the file at pickup time.
slides.footer: Goal: money issues escalate before move-in day

slides.title: Make-ready status has to feed the resident workflow.
slides.body: Cleaning, repairs, inspection completion, vendor delays, and final approval should update the move-in lane automatically instead of living in separate maintenance threads.
slides.footer: Goal: resident messaging reflects real unit status

slides.title: Late documents or failed readiness checks need a named owner immediately.
slides.body: Missing insurance, utility gaps, payment problems, unresolved repairs, or lease exceptions should route with summary, deadline, and next action attached.
slides.footer: Goal: exception paths do not hide inside reminders

slides.title: Move-in status belongs in the CRM or PMS your team already runs from.
slides.body: Readiness stage, missing items, latest resident confirmation, unit status, and next owner should write back so the team is not rebuilding context on move-in morning.
slides.footer: Goal: one record shows what is done and what is blocking keys
